Honda Australia is recalling 528 examples of its HR-V and ZR-V SUVs, as well as its Civic hatchback, to fix an issue that could lead to a flat battery. “Due to a manufacturing issue, the Body Control Module (BCM) may not switch to power-saving mode after the ignition is turned off and the doors are locked. As a result, the battery may gradually discharge if the vehicle is parked for an extended period,” the official recall notice said. “If the battery discharges after the vehicle is parked for an extended period, the vehicle may not start. “The affected vehicles do not comply with Australian Design Rule (ADR) 82/00 – Engine Immobilisers.” CarExpert can help you research, compare and buy so you choose with confidence. The VIN list shows 484 of the recalled vehicles are HR-V SUVs, along with 22 ZR-Vs and 22 Civics. Honda Australia also recalled Civic, ZR-V and Accord vehicles in September 2026 due to front seat frames that may not meet Australian Design Rule requirements. The Accord was also recalled in November 2025 over a software issue. Honda Australia will contact owners of affected vehicles in writing, asking them to book an appointment with their local Honda dealer to have the issue fixed, free of charge. title: Liverpool Player Ratings v Manchester United: Ngumoha & Wirtz Crucial To Victory - Yahoo Sports
content: Liverpool delivered a devastating performance against rivals Manchester United, winning 4-0 and pushing themselves back into the top four of the Premier League. An early red card for Leny Yoro set the tone for the rest of the game, as Dominik Szoboszlai punished immediately via a free kick. Florian Wirtz doubled the lead minutes later with a cheeky volleyed finish with his weaker foot before two second-half goals from Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz sealed victory on derby day at Anfield. The Reds' shot-stopper had very little to do, with almost all of the game being played at the other end of the pitch. Wasn't tested much defensively, but had a couple aimless balls into the box in a quiet game for the full-back. Given the numerical advantage Liverpool had, the defence wasn't challenged much, but the few corners that United had, Virgil Van Dijk dealt with well, and he won the ball back for the Reds' fourth of the game. A couple of crucial tackles when the away side hit LFC on the counterattack, in an otherwise uneventful game for the young centre-half. The Uruguayan played the ball in behind, which resulted in Leny Yoro getting sent off, and mopped up any threat that Patrick Dorgu posed, especially in the first half. Another top draw display from Liverpool's number 10, he played line-breaking balls through the United defence and kept play moving in the middle of the field. Took his free kick superbly well, giving Senne Lammens no chance to save it. Continued to have shots from range, testing the goalkeeper, and, as always, the energy he brought was exceptional. Once again, the 18-year-old starboy was arguably the most dangerous player on the pitch, and he had his full-back beaten time after time. A goal and an assist this afternoon, and for the full 78 minutes he was on the pitch, he was incredible. The only player who had a better game than the young England international was Florian Wirtz. Off the back of a strong international campaign with Germany, Wirtz came back to Anfield full of confidence and played his best game in an LFC shirt to date. Like Ngumoha, a goal and an assist, but had players around him converted their chances, he could have left this fixture with another two or three goal contributions. Playing on the right hand side for most of the game, Bradley Barcola was being overshadowed by the attacking players around him for most of the game, but shortly before he was withdrawn, he ran in behind and provided the assist for Ngumoha's goal. A goalless game for Liverpool's Swedish striker, but his off-the-ball work and overall link-up play were the best they have been in a Red shirt. He looked sharp and was very unlucky not to get at least a goal, if not more, so despite not getting on the scoresheet, Iraola will be pleased with his number nine's display. He came on for the last 20 minutes and added fresh legs in the middle of the pitch when the game was becoming stretched. The Spaniard was clinical with his chance, created by Wirtz, showing a composure and a focus to impact the game from the bench, regardless of how in control his side was in this contest. Came on playing as a winger, but had little to do going forward or defending in the 10 minutes he was on. Allowed Iraola to bring off Ronald Araujo and make sure he is available for an away trip to Belgium midweek. The game was done before the Welsh forward took to the pitch. The German playmaker was exceptional today, and continued his glittering form that began before the international break, carried on while with Jurgen Klopp and Germany, playing a crucial role in LFC winning so convincingly. And it is clear that if Andoni Iraola can keep Wirtz fit and in form, he will be a huge difference maker as this season progresses.

title: Liverpool v Manchester United: How the players rated - BBC
content: Mauricio Pochettino's reign as Manchester United manager got off to a dismal start as his side were beaten 4-0 by rivals Liverpool after playing 82 minutes with 10 men. Here's how BBC Sport rated the players - and you can see how you scored them below. Alisson Becker: Caught one cross and took a few goal-kicks. Made a good save to deny Bruno Fernandes in stoppage time. Had little else to do. 6 Ronald Araujo: Never really tested defensively. Made a few contributions going forward. 7 Jeremy Jacquet: Went shoulder to shoulder with Bryan Mbeumo in the box at 0-0, although a penalty against the French defender would have been harsh. 6 Virgil van Dijk: Organised the defence well. Had some nice link-ups with Rio Ngumoha. 7 Dominik Szoboszlai: Fantastic driven free-kick to open the scoring. Went close a few more times with long shots and generally bossed the midfield. 8 Alexis Mac Allister: Did all the simple things right and allowed others to shine around him. Forced Senne Lammens into a top save in the first half. 7 Bradley Barcola: Missed a few chances to score his first league goal for Liverpool when through one-vs-one. Showed his electric pace to set up his side's third. 7 Florian Wirtz: Readjusted well to net Liverpool's second and assisted their fourth. Five goals in four games for club and country now and looks close to his creative best. 8 Rio Ngumoha: So direct and skilful. Scored Liverpool's third with a calm finish. Also set up their second after easily beating Diogo Dalot. Club and country have a real talent on their hands. 9 Alexander Isak: Led the line well but missed some big chances. Won the free-kick that resulted in Szoboszlai's goal and led to Leny Yoro's sending off. 6 Victor Munoz (on 72, Barcola): Good cameo and took his goal well, curling it into the far corner. 7 Trey Nyoni (on 72, Mac Allister): Looked bright. Had a shot go just over. 6 Subs not used: Chiesa, Mamardashvili, McConell, Tsimikas. Senne Lammens: Could he have done better with the opener? Good save to deny Mac Allister and some decent stops after that. 6 Leny Yoro: Did he have to make the tackle on Isak? It was almost as though he thought about whether he should and decided the answer was yes. Given Liverpool scored from the free-kick it was a bad decision. 4 Matthijs de Ligt: First Premier League start in almost 12 months in middle of a back three turned into a nightmare with the early error that led to opening goal and Yoro red card. Struggled from that moment on. 4 Lisandro Martinez: Fully extended by Liverpool's attack. The least bad of the visitors' starting defence, but that isn't saying much. Exposed completely by Barcola for Liverpool's third. 5 Diogo Dalot: Given a torrid time by Ngumoha, which prompted Pochettino to bring on Maguire. Tries hard but it's not enough. 5 Youri Tielemans: Concerns about a midfield partnership with Mainoo emerge again. Not having the sustained impact required for a player of his experience. 4 Kobbie Mainoo: Twenty-one-year-old being asked to shoulder so much responsibility in an ailing team. New midfield recruits have not helped him. 5 Bryan Mbeumo: Couple of decent bursts came to nothing, then sacrificed after Yoro red card. Received consoling pat on the head from his new boss. 5 Bruno Fernandes: Early free-kick just wide and shot straight at Alisson. Given the carnage at Old Trafford this season, no wonder contract talks on hold. Furious at free-kick given against him when he thought he was through. 5 Patrick Dorgu: Asked to do an awful lot, initially as wing-back, then further back. Lucky Barcola fluffed his lines or his failure to keep an offside line would have been exposed. 5 Matheus Cunha: Tried to keep simmering frustration in check. Not easy in a losing side with no service. Replaced at the break. 5 Harry Maguire (on 22, Mbeumo): Couldn't have expected to be called on so soon. Went into middle of back three and immediately blocked an Isak effort to prevent a third goal. Tried hard. 5 Joshua Zirkzee (on 46, Cunha): Pre-match rumours of a rare start proved unfounded. Replaced Cunha at half-time and asked to bring a different skillset to the number nine role. More physical but not as good and lost possession too easily. 4 Mason Mount (on 65, Tielemans): Only on for a couple of minutes when attempted crossfield pass went to Liverpool player and eventually a third goal. 5 Noussair Mazraoui (on 65, Dorgu): Not really sure what he was supposed to do. Tried to push forward as United's poor control brought more pressure. 4 The red card that changed Liverpool-Man Utd: correct call? title: Czechia v Canada: Preview - Davis Cup
content: The opening tie of the 2026 Davis Cup by Generali Final 8 in Bologna pits Czechia against Canada for the very first time. While Canada seeks to make a first semi-final since winning it all in 2022, it’s been an even longer road back for the Czechs, who have been shut out of the semi-finals for over a decade. The two sides will play three matches - two singles followed by a deciding doubles, if required. The winner will face either Italy or Korea, Rep. in Friday’s semifinal. This will be the debut meeting for Czechia and Canada. Team: Jiri Lehecka, Jakub Mensik, Tomas Machac, Patrik Rikl, Adam Pavlasek History: Champions for the first time in 1980, Czechia became a Davis Cup powerhouse at the end of the 2000s, roaring into their first final in nearly three decades in 2009. Three years later, they won the first of two back-to-back titles in 2012 and 2013. Led by future captain Tomas Berdych, the Czechs earned thrilling 3-2 wins over Spain and Serbia, with both ties coming down to the final rubber. Their 2014 bid for a three-peat ended in the semifinals, and by the end of the decade, they had fallen out of the World Group entirely. Back on the main stage in Bologna, the Czechs bring a strong line-up to the Finals after a pair of wins in the qualifiers. In September, Jiri Lehecka and Jakub Mensik teamed up to defeat the United States for a second year in a row to book their ticket to the Final 8. One to watch: Jiri Lehecka carries plenty of energy into the Davis Cup Finals after a slew of quality results this fall. The 25-year-old made his first Masters 1000 final at the Miami Open and made two more finals in the last month. With a 14-7 record in Davis Cup singles matches, Lehecka is 3-0 in 2026, scoring crucial victories over Ben Shelton and Learner Tien to lead Czechia into the Finals. Team: Felix Auger-Aliassime, Liam Draxl, Alexis Galarneau, Duncan Chan, Keegan Rice History: Canada first joined Davis Cup in 1913 and finally came of age in 2022 when they lifted their first-ever Davis Cup trophy. The victory was a culmination of a ten-year climb that began in 2013, when they shocked Spain en route to the semifinals. They fell just short of the title in 2019 but got their revenge just three years later when Felix Auger-Aliassime scored a key win over Carlos Alcaraz in group play, who rode that momentum to a flawless performance in the knockout stage. After nearly falling out of the World Group in 2025, Canada is back in the mix in 2026, winning two home ties over Brazil and France. Against the latter, Auger-Aliassime nabbed decisive wins over Quentin Halys and Arthur Rinderknech. One to watch: Speaking of Auger-Aliassime, the 26-year-old proved toughest to beat indoors this season, winning his ninth career singles title in Montpellier and reaching a 22nd career final the following week in Rotterdam. Peaking at No. 4 in the rankings in June, the Montreal native will aim to end his 2026 season on a high note against the likes of Lehecka and Mensik, against whom he owns a combined 4-2 head-to-head. title: Ireland v Springboks: Winners and losers as 'big men' dominate and South African fans forced to eat 'humble pie' - Planet Rugby
content: Ireland centre Stuart McCloskey and Springboks back-row Marco van Staden (inset) were in the thick of the action in Dublin. Ireland beat the Springboks 20-17 in a tightly fought contest at the Aviva Stadium on Saturday, in the final round of the Nations Championship pool stage. Selected to start at inside centre ahead of Bundee Aki, the Ulsterman was excellent in the carry, beating four defenders to give the home side the physical advantage in attack. Defensively, he was solid, eventually teaming up with fellow big man Aki in the second half to smother the Springboks‘ attack. Again, Franco Mostert defied his age, getting all over the park in another tremendously hard-working display. His superpower, besides being two metres tall, is his ability to work harder than almost anyone else on the field, and he exhausted himself with an impressive 15 completed tackles in just 43 minutes. Excellent in the lineout again, but it was his work in open play that set him apart, carrying the ball nine times and putting in a serious shift in the breakdown. His try midway through the second half was less about being in the right place at the right time, but more a result of his heavy involvement throughout. Another two tries in the bag for the elusive Irish winger. He was again excellent with ball in hand, using his impressive finishing abilities to give Ireland an early lead. Although he failed to register any more points on the scoreboard, he continued to harass the South African line throughout, carrying the ball 15 times, breaking the line twice, beating three defenders and making over 50 metres. The 23-year-old playmaker was cleared to face the Springboks earlier in the week after a foul play charge from Ireland’s win over Fiji was dismissed. Prendergast put that incident behind him andput in a solid all-round display against the world champions. He missed some shots at goal but his tactical kicking was of a high standard while he also impressed with his playmaking skills and will be hoping to build on this performance when Ireland face Australia next week. The 24-year-old is truly starting to make the shirt his own in Jasper Wiese’s absence. Although he wasn’t quite as flashy as he’s been in previous appearances, he proved a nuisance in the breakdown, winning some really important ball for his scrum-half, Morne van den Berg. He may still be fresh to the international arena, but he’s playing as though he’s been involved for years. Once again, he was terrific around the base of the ruck, leading all of the Springboks‘ attack, and was incredibly strong in the contact area. Although the 28-year-old was overshadowed by fellow Ireland winger Baloucoune, he came to the fore with an impressive all-round performance. Hansen was in the thick of the action from the outset as he took the fight to the Springboks with ball in hand while also doing well under the high ball. His attacking efforts saw him finishing this clash with 37 metres gained which included four defenders beaten. He was forced off the field early on with an injury, summing up what has been an uncharacteristically poor autumn for him. Go back three months, and he was overwhelmingly regarded as the best full-back in the game, particularly with Thomas Ramos out injured, but his form has certainly dwindled, and a spot out with injury certainly won’t help. After hurling a barrage of abuse at officials following their loss to France last week, Springbok fans will be forced to eat humble pie following their side’s loss on Saturday. No refereeing decisions can be blamed for their defeat to Ireland, who, simply put, were the better team on the day. A sharp grounding for the most successful team of the past decade. The Springboks boss was forced to watch the game on television after accusing officials of “match-fixing” last week. But in true Rassie fashion, he’s made headlines again after potentially breaching his ban by allegedly speaking to his coaching team during the match. Erasmus hosted a ‘watch party’ with fans, but had his microphone muted for the entire first half and was seen speaking with earbuds in his ears while covering his mouth and reaching for his phone multiple times. A couple of mistakes here and there wouldn’t have been the end of the world, but being turned over four times certainly won’t be a statistic that he’ll look back on with any fondness. In some matches, losing possession won’t hurt, but against the world champions, it’s a risk that needs to be removed. Marco van Staden was yellow-carded with eight minutes remaining on the clock. The main problem: it was totally preventable and completely unneeded. The Irish had won a ruck and were setting up the caterpillar before Van Staden threw his shoulder into the head of the sealing Irishman, reducing the Springboks to 14 men. In the same phase of play as Van Staden’s dismissal, Dan Sheehan performed a croc roll of sorts, taking his marching orders alongside Van Staden. With such close attention on these ruck incidents nowadays, to do it so obviously and at such a crucial time will have infuriated his coaches. When will the young fly-half step up and have a genuinely good game against a top-level nation? There’s no doubting his immense talent, but his ability to control a game and shine at the highest level is yet to be realised. Against Ireland, he struggled to control the match, allowing his scrum-half to dictate play while he sat back and watched as the Springboks’ attack continued without him. If he’s to have the career that the likes of Handre Pollard and Morne Steyn had in a Springbok jersey, he needs to start work on his game management. title: Ireland player ratings v South Africa: Rob Baloucoune puts in stunning display - The Irish Times

title: Man City 1-1 Fulham: How the players rated - BBC
content: Elliot Anderson scored his second goal of the season for Manchester City Elliot Anderson's stunning second-half volley rescued a point against Fulham, but Manchester City extend their winless run to four games in the Premier League. Here's how I rated the players, and how you rated the players. Gianluigi Donnarumma: Has been in poor form recently but could do nothing about the opener. Made a very important save to deny Rodrigo Muniz. 6 Abdukodir Khusanov: Not a natural right-back and noticeable at times, cutting back instead of marauding forward with ball at his feet. 6 Ruben Dias: Another game where captain Dias and his side have failed to keep a clean sheet. 6 Marc Guehi: Missed England's recent matches through injury but did not look in any trouble in this game. 7 Nico O'Reilly: Almost scored at one end and could have given one away at the other when he tried to play for offside. 6 Ayyoub Bouaddi: Given a start in place of Enzo Fernandez and grew in the second half but was he able to fully grasp his opportunity? 7 Elliot Anderson: The pick of the home players when his side needed him the most. Covered every blade of grass and equalised with a sensational volley. 9 Iliman Ndiaye: Needs to start stepping up. Created very little and hasn't really shone in the absence of Antoine Semenyo. 6 Jeremy Doku: Another who has to start performing.
